inlines.v: RENOUNCE, verb transitive renouns'. [Latin renuncio; re and nuncio, to declare, from the root of nomen, name.] 1. To disown; to disclaim; to reject; as a title or claim; to refuse to own or acknowledge as belonging to; as, to renounce a title to land or a claim to reward; to renounce all pretensions to applause. 2. To deny; to cast off; to reject; to disclaim; as an obligation or duty; as, to renounce allegiance. 3. To cast off or reject, as a connection or possession; to forsake; as, to renounce the world and all its cares. We have renounced the hidden things of dishonesty. 2 Corinthians 4:2. RENOUNCE, verb intransitive renouns'. To declare a renunciation. He of my sons who falls to make it good, by one rebellious act renounces to my blood. [Not in use.] RENOUNCE, noun renouns'. The declining to follow suit, when it can be done.
